Clinic seizures\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOsce questions\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1) Reasons for seizures in old age people\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Neurodegenerative disorders\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Cerebrovascular disorders\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Dementia\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Metabolic disorders\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; - Hypoglycemia\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; - electrolyte imbalances\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; - uraemia\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Physical or mental exhaustion\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2) pathophysiology of seizures\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* To function normally brain must maintain a continual balance between excitation and inhibition , remaining responsive to environment while avoiding continued unrestrained\u0026nbsp; spontaneous activity\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* GABA inhibitory neurotransmitter acts on ion channels , enhances inflow of chloride and reduces formation of action potential\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Excitatory amino acids allow\u0026nbsp; influx of sodium and calcium and producing opposite effects\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* It is likely that many seizures results from an imbalance between this excitation and inhibition.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"letter-spacing: 0.2px;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;( From Davidson medicine text book )\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"letter-spacing: -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"letter-spacing: 0.2px;\"\u003E- It delays recovery of sodium ion channels from inactivated state , thereby reduces neuronal activity\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"letter-spacing: 0.2px;\"\u003E- It exhibits dose dependent elimination , so therapeutic monitoring of phenytoin is essential for adjustment of dosage\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"letter-spacing: 0.2px;\"\u003E- It has dose dependent toxicity\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"letter-spacing: 0.2px;\"\u003E- Adverse effects : Hypersensitivity reactions, hypertrophy and hyperplasia of gum , hyperglycemia , osteomalacia\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELevetiracetam\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- not exactly known , binds to synaptic vesicle protein and modulates release of neurotransmitters like GABA\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Adverse effects : sedation , dizziness , fatigue\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E— points to be noted in a case of epilepsy presenting in old age\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* The late onset epilepsy is very common\u0026nbsp; and incidence in those over 60 is rising\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* The antiepileptic drug regimen should be kept as simple as possible and care should be taken to avoid drug interactions being prescribed\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Withdrawal of antiepileptic should be attempted only where benefits exceed risk of harm from seizures.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"letter-spacing: line-height: 1.6em; margin: 1.5em 0px 2em;\"\u003EThis is an online e log book to discuss our patient de-identified health data shared after taking his \/ her \/ guardians signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input.\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI have been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \" patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and come up with diagnosis and treatment plan.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 65yr old female resident of lingotum with history of seizures\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EChief complaints:-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"letter-spacing: 0.2px;\"\u003E.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient was brought with chief complaints of Active involuntary movements 5 days back, history of frothing , mouth deviation to left\u0026nbsp; uprolling eyeball ,no h\/o of tongue bite, urinary incontinence, fever, head injury, vomitings, loose stools.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS:-\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 11 days back later she developed her first episode of seizure with sudden onset of movements in upper and lower limbs for 5 minutes.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu\u003EThe episode\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/u\u003Ebegan with headache and dizziness, up-rolling of the eyes followed by loss of consciousness and uncontrolled involuntary movements of the arms and legs, clasping of the hands and deviation of the mouth to one side. She regained consciousness 5-10 minutes later in a confused state, with no memory of the episode. She was brought to the hospital by her son where she was prescribed levetiracetam and she left the day after.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESecond episode began in the night time 5 days back (on 2\/12\/23) and\u0026nbsp; had complaints of headache dragging type pain radiating to neck . This was followed by up-rolling of the eyeballs loss of consciousness and sudden onset of involuntary movements,\u0026nbsp; frothing,\u0026nbsp; deviation of mouth towards left and confusion in postictal period.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"letter-spacing: 0.2px;\"\u003ENo h\/o episode of seizure activity after bringing to casualty\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eno h\/o of involuntary defecation\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eno h\/o fever, cough, vomitings, loose stools, pain in abdomen.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPAST HISTORY:-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESimilar episode 5 days ago for which she visited a local hospital
